tour.name: Project Onboarding: Architecture & Configuration
tour.description: Start here if you're new to the codebase. This tour walks through the project documentation, configuration files, and overall architecture to help you understand how the system is organized.

steps.description: Read the project overview, setup instructions, and architecture diagram to understand the system's purpose and high-level design.
Examine the main configuration entry point to see how environment variables and application settings are loaded and managed.
Review database connection settings, ORM configuration, and connection pooling strategies.
Understand the testing framework configuration, coverage thresholds, and module path mappings.
Learn about test environment initialization, global mocks, and database test setup routines.
See how API routes are aggregated, versioned, and mounted on the Express application.
Explore the service layer organization and dependency injection patterns used throughout the application.
Review the data model registry and understand how entity relationships are defined.

tour.name: Data Layer: Models & Repositories
tour.description: Learn how data is structured and accessed. This tour covers the data models, repository pattern implementation, and how the service layer interacts with data stores.

steps.description: Study the core user entity with its fields, validation rules, and relationships to other models.
Examine a more complex model demonstrating associations, enums, and business constraints.
Understand the repository pattern implementation, query methods, and transaction management for user data.
Learn advanced repository techniques including complex joins, pagination, and bulk operations.
Review connection pooling, migration configuration, and seeding strategies for the data layer.
See how the service layer consumes repositories to implement business operations and maintain data consistency.
Examine database migration scripts and understand how the schema evolves over time.

tour.name: Service Layer: Business Logic & Orion Integration
tour.description: Explore the service layer where business logic lives, including the Orion platform service for external integrations. Learn how services orchestrate operations and maintain separation of concerns.

steps.description: Study the service pattern implementation, transaction management, and core business rules for user operations.
Understand authentication business logic, token management, and security implementations.
Learn how the Orion platform service is initialized and integrated into the application ecosystem.
Examine the HTTP client implementation, retry mechanisms, circuit breakers, and error handling for external API calls.
Discover how cross-cutting concerns like notifications are handled through event-driven patterns.
Review service initialization scripts and environment bootstrapping procedures.
Analyze complex business workflows, state machines, and multi-step orchestration in the service layer.

tour.name: API Layer: Routes, Controllers & Middleware
tour.description: Understand how HTTP requests are processed. This tour covers middleware for auth and validation, controllers for request handling, and route definitions for API endpoints.

steps.description: Examine JWT validation, permission checks, and the authentication middleware pipeline.
Learn how request validation is performed using schemas, sanitization, and type coercion.
Study centralized error handling, custom error classes, and consistent response formatting.
Understand the controller pattern, request/response mapping, and HTTP status code handling.
Trace the login, registration, and token refresh flows through the controller layer.
Review route definitions, versioning strategies, route grouping, and parameter handling.
See how routers are composed, middleware is mounted, and CORS is configured at the application level.

tour.name: Testing & Coverage Analysis
tour.description: Learn the testing strategy, how to run tests, and interpret coverage reports. This tour covers unit tests, integration tests, and coverage analysis for different modules.

steps.description: Understand test configuration, coverage thresholds, module name mapping, and test environment settings.
Review test environment setup, global mocks, database test fixtures, and test utility functions.
Study service layer unit testing patterns, mock implementations, and assertion strategies.
Learn controller testing using Supertest for HTTP assertions and mocking service dependencies.
Examine integration testing approaches that test the full request/response cycle through middleware and controllers.
Analyze the coverage report for core modules to identify well-tested and under-tested areas.
Review coverage analysis for asynchronous queue processing and background job handlers.
Examine coverage metrics specifically for API key authentication and project-scoped operations.

tour.name: End-to-End Request Flow
tour.description: Trace a complete user request through all layers, from HTTP request to database and back. Perfect for understanding how the pieces fit together and where to debug issues.

steps.description: Request enters the application here. Observe how routes are matched and middleware stacks are assembled.
Authentication middleware validates the JWT token and attaches user context to the request.
Input validation middleware sanitizes and validates request payloads against defined schemas.
Controller receives the validated request, invokes the appropriate service method, and formats the response.
Service layer executes business logic, validates business rules, and coordinates repository calls.
Repository builds and executes database queries, handling transactions and connection management.
Data model defines the schema, relationships, and serialization logic for the returned data.
Response passes through error handling middleware before being sent to the client.

issues.message: Graph has only 6 edges for 68 nodes (average degree 0.18). This is severely underconnected for a layered architecture knowledge graph.
No dependency edges between layers (e.g., API→Service, Service→Data) are present or accounted for in the 6-edge count. A layered architecture requires these fundamental relationships.
Only ~15 modules explicitly listed across all layers, but graph contains 68 nodes. Approximately 82% of nodes (53 nodes) have no defined layer assignment.
Within listed modules, there are no visible edges connecting related components (e.g., routes→controllers, controllers→services, services→repositories).
Testing layer contains configuration files and coverage artifacts (.coverage-*, jest.config.js, jest.setup.js) which are typically not conceptual graph nodes but rather metadata or build artifacts.

suggestions: Add dependency edges between layers: API depends on Service, Service depends on Data, Utility supports all layers
Add intra-layer edges: routes→controllers, controllers→service modules, services→repositories, models→repositories
Provide complete node definitions to verify all 68 nodes are properly categorized
Add relationship types such as 'depends_on', 'calls', 'imports', or 'contains'
Consider whether configuration files and coverage artifacts should be excluded from the graph or treated as metadata attributes
Target edge count should be proportional to node count; for 68 nodes, expect 100+ edges in a meaningful architecture graph
Add cross-cutting relationships for middleware, config, and scripts that span multiple layers
